title: The Binomial Theorem
seo_title: Binomial Theorem Worksheet: Pascal's Triangle and Expansions | 100 Questions with Answers
standard_text: Know and apply the Binomial Theorem for the expansion of (x + y)ⁿ in powers of x and y for a positive integer n, where x and y are any numbers, with coefficients determined for example by Pascal's Triangle.
meta_desc: Free precalculus worksheet on the binomial theorem: binomial coefficients, Pascal's triangle, finding a term, full expansions and coin-flip probabilities. 100 questions.
key_big: (x + y)ⁿ has n + 1 terms with coefficients nCk from Pascal's triangle.
key_sub: Raise the whole term, sign included, to each power.
body_html:
How it works

  • Binomial theorem: (x + y)n = Σ nCk xn−kyk, for k = 0 to n.
  • nCk = n! / (k!(n − k)!), the numbers in row n of Pascal's triangle.
  • There are n + 1 terms. In each term, the exponents add to n.
  • For (ax + b)n, raise the whole first term and the whole second term (with its sign) to their powers.
Example

Find the coefficient of x³ in (2x − 1)5.

The term is 5C2(2x)³(−1)²

= 10 · 8 · 1

Answer: 80

Example

Expand (x + 2)³.

Row 3: 1, 3, 3, 1

x³ + 3x²(2) + 3x(4) + 8

Answer: x³ + 6x² + 12x + 8

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to raise the coefficient: (2x)³ = 8x³, not 2x³.
  • Losing the sign: (−1)² = 1 but (−1)³ = −1.
  • Using the wrong row or position in Pascal's triangle.
  • Counting n terms. (x + y)n has n + 1 terms.

faq.a: It expands (x + y)ⁿ as a sum of terms nCk · xⁿ⁻ᵏ · yᵏ for k = 0, 1, …, n.

faq.q: How is Pascal's triangle related to the binomial theorem?
faq.a: Row n of Pascal's triangle gives the coefficients of (x + y)ⁿ. Each entry is the sum of the two entries above it.

faq.q: How do you find one term without expanding everything?
faq.a: Choose k so the powers match, then compute nCk times the first term to the power n − k times the second term to the power k.

faq.q: How do you find the sum of the coefficients?
faq.a: Substitute x = 1 (and y = 1) into the binomial. For (2x − 1)⁵, the sum is (2 − 1)⁵ = 1.

A fair coin is flipped 10 times. What is the probability of exactly 8 heads?
items.e: There are 10C8 = 45 ways to place the heads among 1024 equally likely outcomes (210). 45/1024 = 451024.

items.q: A fair coin is flipped 5 times. What is the probability of exactly 4 heads?
items.e: There are 5C4 = 5 ways to place the heads among 32 equally likely outcomes (25). 5/32 = 532.
